2. This application is filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963 for condonation of delay of 1318 days in preferring the First Appeal.

sentences.text: 3. Heard learned advocate for applicants and learned AGP for respondent-State.

4. It is submitted that the preset First Appeal is arising out of Land Acquisition Reference Case No.252 of 1995 wherein group of LAR Nos.244 to 258 of 1995 and allied matters, delay has been condoned.

entities.text: Land Acquisition Reference Case No.252 of 1995
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: The present First Appeal is arising out of the Land Reference Case No.252 of 1995.

5. It is submitted that the order dated 17.07.2023 passed by the Coordinate Bench of this Court in the matter i.e. Civil Application for Condonation of Delay No.1 of 2023 in F/First Appeal No.6287 of 2023 which is taken on record.

entities.text: Civil Application for Condonation of Delay No.1 of 2023
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: Since the First Appeal is arising out of the same group of matters and further submitted that delay may be condoned.

6. Learned advocate for the applicants submitted that the applicants are not much literate and are a poor small agriculturists and further submitted that the applicants are not aware about the NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/733/2024 ORDER DATED: 12/02/2024 undefined procedure of the Court of law.

He has placed reliance on decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of K.
Subbarayadu and others Vs. The Special Deputy Collector (Land Acquisition) reported in 2017(12)
SCC 840 and would submit that considering the law laid down in aforementioned case, the applicants are not claiming their right for the interest upon the enhanced compensation, if any, for the delay period.

entities.text:
K.
Subbarayadu and others Vs. The Special Deputy Collector (Land Acquisition) reported in 2017(12)
SCC 840
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the delay is not intentional and there was no lethargy on the part of the applicants.
7. Per contra, there is an objection on the part of the learned AGP that the delay has not been sufficiently explained and therefore, present application may be dismissed.

8. Applying the ratio of aforestated judgment in background of the facts of the present case as well as considering the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of K. Subbarayadu (Supra), the application seeking condonation of delay deserves consideration.
However, the claimant would not be entitled to claim interest on the enhanced amount of compensation, if any, during the delay period.
9. In view of the above, this Court is of the opinion that the delay NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/733/2024 ORDER DATED: 12/02/2024 undefined has sufficiently been explained.
